sanskrit: agne acchā vadeha naḥ pratyaṅ naḥ sumanā bhava | pra no yaccha viśas pate dhanadā asi nas tvam ||
english: O Agni, speak here toward us; turn to us with favour, be well-disposed. Bestow gifts upon us, O Lord of the clan — for it is thou who art the giver of wealth to us.

sanskrit: pra no yacchatv aryamā pra bhagaḥ pra bṛhaspatiḥ | pra devāḥ prota sūnṛtā rāyo devī dadātu naḥ ||
english: May Aryamā bestow gifts upon us, may Bhaga, may Bṛhaspati; may the gods bestow, and also Sūnṛtā — may the divine lady of riches give to us.

sanskrit: somaṁ rājānam avase 'gniṁ gīrbhir havāmahe | ādityān viṣṇuṁ sūryam brahmāṇaṁ ca bṛhaspatim ||
english: We invoke King Soma for our aid, and Agni with our songs; the Ādityas, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, and Brahmāṇaspati.

sanskrit: indravāyū bṛhaspatiṁ suhaveha havāmahe | yathā naḥ sarva ij janaḥ saṁgatyāṁ sumanā asat ||
english: Indra-and-Vāyu, and Bṛhaspati — we invoke them here with easy invocation, so that every person in the assembly may be well-disposed toward us.

sanskrit: aryamaṇam bṛhaspatim indraṁ dānāya codaya | vātaṁ viṣṇuṁ sarasvatīṁ savitāraṁ ca vājinam ||
english: Urge Aryaman, Bṛhaspati, and Indra to bestow gifts; urge Vāta, Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī, and Savitṛ, the impeller of prizes.

sanskrit: tvaṁ no agne agnibhir brahma yajñaṁ ca vardhaya | tvaṁ no devatātaye rāyo dānāya codaya ||
english: Do thou, O Agni, increase our prayer and sacrifice with thy fires; do thou impel the gods to come and wealth to be given to us.

sanskrit: ayam agne jaritā tve abhūd api sahasaḥ sūno nahy anyad asty āpyam | bhadraṁ hi śarma trivarūtham asti ta āre hiṁsānām apa didyum ā kṛdhi ||
english: This praiser, O Agni, O son of strength, has become dependent on thee — there is indeed no other refuge. For thy shelter is threefold and beneficent; keep far from us the gleam of those who would harm.

sanskrit: pravat te agne janimā pitūyataḥ sācīva viśvā bhuvanā ny ṛñjase | pra saptayaḥ pra saniṣanta no dhiyaḥ puraś caranti paśupā iva tmanā ||
english: Thy birth is on the downward slope, O Agni, as thou seekest nourishment; like a companion thou dost embrace all beings. Let our seven hymns go forward and win prizes; they move in front, of their own accord, like a keeper of cattle.

sanskrit: uta vā u pari vṛṇakṣi bapsad bahor agna ulapa svadhāvaḥ | uta khilyā urvarāṇām bhavanti mā te hetiṁ taviṣīṁ cukrudhāma ||
english: Or thou dost devour all around with thy devouring mouth, O Agni of the thicket — thou who art self-sustaining; and the clumps become the cleared fields of the fertile tracts. May we not have provoked thy terrible missile.

sanskrit: yad udvato nivato yāsi bapsat pṛthag eṣi pragardhinīva senā | yadā te vāto anuvāti śocir vapteva śmaśru vapasi pra bhūma ||
english: When thou dost devour going over heights and into hollows, thou dost advance in different directions like an insatiable army; when the wind blows with thy blazing, thou dost shave the land, as a barber shaves the beard.

sanskrit: praty asya śreṇayo dadṛśra ekaṁ niyānam bahavo rathāsaḥ | bāhū yad agne anumarmṛjāno nyaṅṅ uttānām anveṣi bhūmim ||
english: His ranks are seen all facing one single way; many are the chariots pursuing the single course. When, O Agni, smoothing thy arms along, thou dost search the upturned earth, bending downward.

sanskrit: ut te śuṣmā jihatām ut te arcir ut te agne śaśamānasya vājāḥ | uc chvañcasva ni nama vardhamāna ā tvādya viśve vasavaḥ sadantu ||
english: Let thy vigour rise up, let thy flame rise up, let the prizes of thee, O Agni, who hast laboured, rise up; rear thyself up and bow down as thou growest — today let all the Vasus take their seat in thee.

sanskrit: apām idaṁ nyayanaṁ samudrasya niveśanam | anyaṁ kṛṇuṣvetaḥ panthāṁ tena yāhi vaśām̐ anu ||
english: This is the downward course of the waters, the resting-place of the ocean; make for thyself another path from here — along that path go thou following the cows.

sanskrit: āyane te parāyaṇe dūrvā rohantu puṣpiṇīḥ | hradāś ca puṇḍarīkāṇi samudrasya gṛhā ime ||
english: On thy coming-path and going-path, may flowering Dūrvā grasses grow; and ponds with lotuses — these are the houses of the ocean.

sanskrit: tyaṁ cid atrim ṛtajuram artham aśvaṁ na yātave | kakṣīvantaṁ yadī punā rathaṁ na kṛṇutho navam ||
english: That Atri, made old by truth, swift to the goal as a horse to be driven — even Kakṣīvant, do ye two renew him as if making a chariot new.

sanskrit: tyaṁ cid aśvaṁ na vājinam areṇavo yam atnata | dṛḻhaṁ granthiṁ na vi ṣyatam atriṁ yaviṣṭham ā rajaḥ ||
english: Him, like a vigorous horse whom the particles of dust had covered — do ye two loosen the firm knot; bring Atri, made most young again, into the light.

sanskrit: narā daṁsiṣṭhāv atraye śubhrā siṣāsataṁ dhiyaḥ | athā hi vāṁ divo narā punaḥ stomo na viśase ||
english: O most wonder-working heroes, resplendent ones, ye two are eager to win hymns for Atri; and now, O men of heaven, a praise-song goes to you in turn for your renown.

sanskrit: cite tad vāṁ surādhasā rātiḥ sumatir aśvinā | ā yan naḥ sadane pṛthau samane parṣatho narā ||
english: That gift of yours and that good-will is conspicuous, O Aśvins of rich bounty — when, O heroes, ye carry us through in the wide assembly-place of our gathering.

sanskrit: yuvam bhujyuṁ samudra ā rajasaḥ pāra īṅkhitam | yātam acchā patātribhir nāsatyā sātaye kṛtam ||
english: Ye two brought Bhujyu, who had been tossed beyond the sea, to the farther shore of the realm of cloud; come hither with winged steeds, O Nāsatyas, made ready for the winning.

sanskrit: ā vāṁ sumnaiḥ śaṁyū iva maṁhiṣṭhā viśvavedasā | sam asme bhūṣataṁ narotsaṁ na pipyuṣīr iṣaḥ ||
english: O most bountiful ones, knowing all things, come to us with your blessings, like beneficent spirits; adorn us, O heroes, with refreshments swelling like a spring.

sanskrit: ayaṁ hi te amartya indur atyo na patyate | dakṣo viśvāyur vedhase ||
english: This immortal drop, O Indra, speeds like a swift horse; this is the power, the all-sustaining life, for the ordainer.

sanskrit: ayam asmāsu kāvya ṛbhur vajro dāsvate | ayam biharty ūrdhvakṛśanam madam ṛbhur na kṛtvyam madam ||
english: This is the wise, Ṛbhu-like, the thunderbolt for the pious worshipper; this bears the exhilaration that makes the hairs stand erect — like Ṛbhu, the exhilaration wrought with skill.

sanskrit: ghṛṣuḥ śyenāya kṛtvana āsu svāsu vaṁsagaḥ | ava dīdhed ahīśuvaḥ ||
english: Eager, practised for the falcon, going to its own proper haunts; it has shone down — the one that incites the serpent-slayer.

sanskrit: yaṁ suparṇaḥ parāvataḥ śyenasya putra ābharat | śatacakraṁ yo 'hyo vartaniḥ ||
english: That which the fair-winged one — the son of the falcon — brought from the distant region: the one of a hundred circles, the track of the serpent.

sanskrit: yaṁ te śyenaś cārum avṛkam padābharat aruṇam mānam andhasaḥ | enā vayo vi tāry āyur jīvasa enā jāgāra bandhutā ||
english: That which the falcon brought to thee with its foot, the lovely, harmless, ruddy measure of the Soma plant — by this, the life-giving power extends over life and living; by this, kinship keeps its vigil.

sanskrit: evā tad indra indunā deveṣu cid dhārayāte mahi tyajaḥ | kratvā vayo vi tāry āyuḥ sukrato kratvā ayam asmad ā sutaḥ ||
english: Thus, O Indra, with the drop, even among the gods, the great vigour is maintained; through wisdom the life-giving force extends over life, O wise one — through wisdom this has been pressed out from us for thee.

sanskrit: imāṁ khanāmy oṣadhiṁ vīrudham balavattamām | yayā sapatnīm bādhate yayā saṁvindate patim ||
english: I dig up this plant, the most powerful of herbs, by which one drives away a rival wife, by which one wins a husband.

sanskrit: uttānaparṇe subhage devajūte sahsvati | sapatnīm me parā dhama patim me kevalaṁ kuru ||
english: O plant with spreading leaves, O auspicious one, propelled by the gods, O powerful one — blow my rival wife away; make my husband mine alone.

sanskrit: uttarāham uttara uttared uttarābhyaḥ | athā sapatnī yā mamādhārā sādharābhyaḥ ||
english: I am the higher, I am higher, I am yet higher than the highest; and the rival wife who is mine — she shall be the lower, lower than the lowest.

sanskrit: nahy asyā nāma gṛbhṇāmi no asmin ramate jane | parām eva parāvataṁ sapatnīṁ gamayāmasi ||
english: I do not even take her name, nor does that person take delight in her — we shall drive the rival wife to the very farthest distance.

sanskrit: aham asmi sahamānātha tvam asi sāsahiḥ | ubhe sahasvatī bhūtvī sapatnīm me sahāvahai ||
english: I am the conquering one, and thou art the utterly vanquishing one; both of us, having become conquering women together, let us overcome my rival wife.

sanskrit: upa te 'dhāṁ sahamānām abhi tvādhāṁ sahīyasā | mām anu pra te mano vatsaṁ gaur iva dhāvatu pathā vār iva dhāvatu ||
english: I have placed the conquering one upon thee; I have overpowered thee with one yet more conquering. May thy mind run after me as a cow after her calf, as water runs along its path.

sanskrit: araṇyāny araṇyāny asau yā preva naśyasi | kathā grāmaṁ na pṛcchasi na tvā bhīr iva vindatī ||
english: O Forest Goddess, O Forest Goddess — thou who seemest to vanish in the distance — why dost thou not ask after the village? Does no fear come upon thee?

sanskrit: vṛṣāravāya vadate yad upāvati ciccikah | āghāṭibhir iva dhāvayann araṇyānir mahīyate ||
english: When the cicada sings in answer to the bell-calling bull, the Forest Goddess is exalted, as if driving on with bells.

sanskrit: uta gāva ivādanty uta veśmeva dṛśyate | uto araṇyāniḥ sāyaṁ śakaṭīr iva sarjati ||
english: It seems as if cattle are grazing; it seems as if a dwelling is visible; and in the evening the Forest Goddess releases, as it were, the sound of creaking carts.

sanskrit: gām aṅgaiṣa ā hvayati dārv aṅgaiṣo apāvadhīt | vasann araṇyānyāṁ sāyam akrukṣad iti manyate ||
english: Here one hears a cow being called; here someone has cut wood; one who dwells in the forest at evening thinks he has heard a shout.

sanskrit: na vā araṇyānir hanti anyaś cen nābhigacchati | svādoḥ phalasya jagdhvāya yathākāmaṁ ni padyate ||
english: The Forest Goddess does not slay anyone unless some other comes upon her; having eaten of the sweet fruit, she lies down at will.

sanskrit: āñjanagandhiṁ surabhim bahvannām akṛṣīvalām | prāham mṛgāṇām mātaram araṇyānim aśaṁsiṣam ||
english: Fragrant with collyrium-scent, sweet-smelling, rich in food, not ploughing — I have praised the Forest Goddess, the mother of wild beasts.

sanskrit: śrat te dadhāmi prathamāya manyave 'han yad vṛtraṁ naryaṁ viver apaḥ | ubhe yat tvā bhavato rodasī anu rejate śuṣmāt pṛthivī cid adrivaḥ ||
english: I place my faith in thy foremost fury, in that day when thou, O manly one, didst cleave Vṛtra and release the waters; when both the worlds trembled at thy vigour, O Indra, and even the earth shook at thee who wearest the stone.

sanskrit: tvam māyābhir anavadya māyinaṁ śravasya tā manasā vṛtram ardayaḥ | tvām in naro vṛṇate gaviṣṭiṣu tvāṁ viśvāsu havyāsv iṣṭiṣu ||
english: Thou, O blameless one, with thy magic powers didst crush Vṛtra the magician by the mind that seeks glory; thee indeed do warriors choose in contests for cattle, thee in all desirable sacrificial rites.

sanskrit: aiṣu cākandhi puruhūta sūriṣu vṛdhāso ye maghavann ānaśur magham | arcanti toke tanaye pariṣṭiṣu medhasātā vājinam ahray e dhane ||
english: Be gladdened, O much-invoked Indra, among these patrons — the thriving ones who, O Maghavan, have attained to bounty; they worship thee the prize-winner in contests for children and offspring, in winning of Soma, in shameless pursuit of wealth.

sanskrit: sa in nu rāyaḥ subhṛtasya cākanad madaṁ yo asya raṁhyaṁ cikētati | tvāvṛdho maghavan dāśvadhvaro makṣū sa vājam bharate dhanā nṛbhiḥ ||
english: He indeed is delighted by the wealth well borne, who perceives the swiftness of it; O Maghavan, he who has grown strong through thee, whose sacrifice is offered, quickly wins the prize and riches through heroic men.

sanskrit: tvaṁ śardhāya mahinā gṛṇāna uru kṛdhi maghavañ śagdhi rāyaḥ | tvaṁ no mitro varuṇo na māyī pitvo na dasma dayase vibhaktā ||
english: Being praised with greatness for the bold troop, make wide space, O Maghavan — be capable of giving riches; thou art our friend, O wonderworker, like Varuṇa the wise; like the food-allotter, thou art gracious in distributing.

sanskrit: suṣvāṇāsa indra stumasi tvā sasavāṁsaś ca tuvinṛmṇa vājam | ā no bhara suvitaṁ yasya cākan tmanā tanā sanuyāma tvotāḥ ||
english: We who have pressed the Soma and have won the prize praise thee, O Indra of mighty powers; bring us the bounty in which thou art pleased — aided by thee, may we win it with body and offspring.

sanskrit: ṛṣvas tvam indra śūra jāto dāsīr viśaḥ sūryeṇa sahyāḥ | guhā hitaṁ guhyaṁ gūḻham apsu bibhṛmasi prasravaṇe na somam ||
english: Thou art exalted, O hero Indra, born to overcome the Dāsa folk with the Sun; we carry the hidden, secret thing concealed in the waters, as the Soma in a flowing stream.

sanskrit: aryo vā giro abhy arca vidvān ṛṣīṇāṁ vipraḥ sumatiṁ cakānaḥ | te syāma ye raṇayanta somai enotā tubhyaṁ rathoḻha bhakṣaiḥ ||
english: Or let the inspired sage, knowing the words of the seers, sing out hymns for thee, desiring thy favour; may we be among those who rejoice thee with Soma draughts, yoked to thee, O chariot-rider, with their shares.

sanskrit: imā brahmendrā tubhyaṁ śaṁsi dā nṛbhyo nṛṇāṁ śūra śavaḥ | tebhir bhava sakratur yeṣu cākann uta trāyasva gṛṇata uta stīn ||
english: These prayers, O Indra, I offer to thee — give heroes' heroic power to the men, O hero; be of one mind with those in whom thou art pleased, and protect both the singer and the women.

sanskrit: śrudhī havam indra śūra pṛthyā uta stavase venyasyārkaiḥ | ā yas te yoniṁ ghṛtavantam asvār ūrmir na nimnair dravayanta vakvāḥ ||
english: Hear the spacious call, O hero Indra, and thou art praised with the hymns of the desirable one; those floods that rush like tidal waves into thy ghee-filled birthplace, making it gleam.

sanskrit: savitā yantraiḥ pṛthivīm aramaṇād askambhane savitā dyām adṛṁhat | aśvam ivādhukṣad dhunim antarikṣam atūrte baddhaṁ savitā samudram ||
english: Savitṛ fixed the earth with supports; Savitṛ propped the sky without a pillar; he milked out the restless atmosphere as if a horse; Savitṛ bound the ocean that is unfathomable.

sanskrit: yatrā samudraḥ skabhito vy aunad apāṁ napāt savitā tasya veda | ato bhūr ata ā utthitaṁ rajo 'to dyāvāpṛthivī aprathetām ||
english: Where the braced ocean spread out, Savitṛ, the Son of the Waters, knows of it; from thence the earth arose, from thence the bright space arose, from thence Heaven-and-Earth expanded.

sanskrit: paścedam anyad abhavad yajatram amartasya bhuvanasya bhūnā | suparṇo aṅga savitur garutmān pūrvo jātaḥ sa u asyānu dharma ||
english: Afterwards there came into being the other sacred thing — by the abundance of the immortal world; the fair-winged Garuḍa was born before Savitṛ himself, and he follows even Savitṛ's law.

sanskrit: gāva iva grāmaṁ yūyudhir ivāśvān vāśreva vatsaṁ sumanā duhānā | patir iva jāyām abhi no ny etu dhartā divaḥ savitā viśvavāraḥ ||
english: As cattle come to the village, as the fighter to the horses, as a lowing cow, milking sweetly, to the calf — may Savitṛ, all-desirable upholder of heaven, come to us like a husband to his wife.

sanskrit: hiraṇyastūpaḥ savitar yathā tvāṅgiraso juhve vāje asmin | evā tvārcan avase vandamānaḥ somasyevāṁśum prati jāgarāham ||
english: O Savitṛ of the golden pillar, as Aṅgiras invoked thee for this prize — so, worshipping and praising thee for aid, I am wakeful toward the shoot of Soma.

sanskrit: samiddhaś cit sam idhyase devebhyo havyavāhana | ādityai rudrair vasubhir na ā gahi mṛḻīkāya na ā gahi ||
english: Though already kindled, thou dost kindle thyself afresh as the bearer of oblations to the gods; come to us with the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus — come to us for our welfare.

sanskrit: imaṁ yajñam idaṁ vaco jujuṣāṇa upāgahi | martāsas tvā samidhāna havāmahe mṛḻīkāya havāmahe ||
english: Rejoicing in this sacrifice and this speech, come near; we mortals invoke thee, O thou who art kindled — we invoke thee for our welfare.

sanskrit: tvām u jātavedasaṁ viśvavāraṁ gṛṇe dhiyā | agne devām̐ ā vaha naḥ priyavratān mṛḻīkāya priyavratān ||
english: Thee, O Jātavedas, thee all-desirable, I praise with my prayer; O Agni, bring to us the gods of beloved rites — for our welfare, those of beloved rites.

sanskrit: agnir devo devānām abhavat purohito 'gnim manuṣyā ṛṣayaḥ sam īdhire | agnim maho dhanasātāv ahaṁ huve mṛḻīkaṁ dhanasātaye ||
english: Agni became the divine priest of the gods; the human sages have kindled Agni; I invoke Agni in the great contest for wealth — for welfare, for the winning of wealth.

sanskrit: agnir atrim bharadvājaṁ gaviṣṭhiram prāvan naḥ kaṇvaṁ trasadasyum āhave | agniṁ vasiṣṭho havate purohito mṛḻīkāya purohitaḥ ||
english: Agni aided Atri, Bharadvāja, and Gaviṣṭhira; he aided Kaṇva and Trasadasyu in battle; Vasiṣṭha, the divine priest, invokes Agni — for welfare, as divine priest.
